intro: ^Welcome inside the Mouth, [player]! Every meal starts its journey right here.
^Your mission: chew, mix, then moisten the food and digest its starch with salivary amylase. Three jobs, one at a time!
swallow_fact: ^Did you see the little drop hanging above the throat? That's the uvula. When you swallow, it closes the way to your nose, so food can't go the wrong way.

b: ^At the gate you predicted that saliva starts turning bread into sugar. You were right!
^At the gate you said saliva just makes the bread wet. It does - and it does something even more surprising.
^At the gate you thought saliva does nothing at all. Surprise - it is one of the mouth's hardest workers!
^Now, what does saliva really do to bread?

explain: ^You selected salivary amylase and cut the long starch chains inside the bread into pairs. Each pair is maltose, a sugar made of two glucose units. That is how saliva starts digesting starch!
^So that's why bread tastes sweet when we chew it for a long time!
^Exactly. Your teeth broke the food, your tongue mixed it, and your saliva softened it and began to digest it. Together they made a soft ball: the bolus.
^Your bolus is on its way down the esophagus... to the Stomach Kingdom!
